title: Signal stewardship and retention plan for inference probes
content:
Purpose and scope:
This note defines a proposal for stewarding inference-related telemetry (metrics, traces, synthetic probes) across short/medium/long retention tiers. Focus is on cost-aware retention, operator utility, regulatory constraints, and reproducible incident reconstruction for Redwood’s inference stack (hosted, dedicated, private).

Objectives (why this matters):
- Keep critical signal available for fast incident investigation (operator-first).
- Reduce storage/query costs by explicit tiering and aggregation rules.
- Provide clear rules for what to sample, what to keep full-fidelity, and when to aggregate.
- Ensure trace/metric retention choices meet privacy/compliance constraints for Private deployments.

Definitions and retention tiers (recommended):
- Live (0-7d): High-cardinality, full-resolution metrics and traces needed for active investigations and rollouts. Retain request-level traces and tokenized debug spans.
- Medium (7-90d): Aggregated and sampled telemetry. Keep detailed traces for a rolling window of important incidents (tagged). Daily-rollup metrics (min/avg/p50/p95/p99) at tenant level preserved.
- Archive (90d-3y): Low-cardinality aggregates and anomaly summaries for long-term trends and ML-quality audits. Store compressed histograms and sparse trace bookmarks only.
- Delete (>3y): Purge unless legally required. Private deployments can set different minima via contract.

Signal classification (quick steward map):
- Critical (S0): SLO/SLA indicators, SRE-facing latencies at p95/p99/p99.9, KV-cache heatmaps, rate limits. Keep in Live and Medium.
- Operational (S1): Batch size distribution, autoscaler signals, host-level GPU metrics. Keep Live (shorter window) and medium aggregated.
- Product/Analytics (S2): Prompt-level quality tags, embedding similarity drift. Store in Medium/Archive for ML drift.
- Ephemeral/Debug (S3): Full prompt text, sampled debug traces. Keep only if flagged; default sampling low and stored Live only.

Canonical metric templates (naming and examples):
- inference.request.latency_ms.p50/p95/p99: Latency from HTTP accept to first token out (ms). Tag by model, route, region, plan_tier, tenant_id (hashed).
- inference.request.token_throughput.mean: avg tokens/sec per request. Tag by model and instance_type.
- inference.kvcache.hit_rate: kv_cache_hits / kv_cache_lookups (0-1). Important for cost attribution.
- inference.batch.size.avg and inference.batch.size.p95: observed batching window size.
- inference.error.rate: errors / total_requests, with error.code tag (e.g., 4xx, 5xx, model-error).
- inference.cost.per_token_usd.estimate: derived, not a raw billing export; used for SLO cost budgets.
Naming rules: snake.case with clear unit suffixes; include pXX percentiles as suffixes.

Metric cardinality and tag guidance:
- Tenant tagging: tenant_id should be hashed or bucketed (e.g., tenant_bucket: 0..255) by default to avoid high cardinality.
- Model and variant: include model.family and model.quant (e.g., gptx-13b.q4_0). Avoid including full commit hashes.
- Route path: use coarse route names (e.g., chat, embeddings, rerank) not full user-provided strings.

Tracing conventions (spans and sampling):
- Span naming: service.operation.resource (e.g., inference.generate.kv_lookup). Keep span names short and consistent.
- Context: Always attach request_id, tenant_bucket, model.family, route, region as span tags. Do NOT attach raw prompt text except on a sampled debug span flagged by policy.
- Severity-weighted sampling: sample 1% of successful requests, 10% for p95+ latency requests, 100% for any request that triggers an error or fallback.
- Breadcrumbs and synthetic bookmarks: when a trace is sampled at high fidelity, create a light-weight bookmark entry zeroing sensitive fields for Archive tier.

Dashboard personas and pane guidance:
- Operator (oncall): Single-pane views showing SLO burn, p95/p99 latency heatmap by region, recent error spike traces, KV-cache warmth. Fast filter for tenant_bucket and model.family.
- SRE (investigation): Loose dashboards with session-replay links, top offending spans, batch-size distribution, and trace replay hooks. Include quick query buttons for 'tail traces last 1h'.
- Product / ML (trend): Drift dashboards with embedding distance histograms, quality annotation rate, and cost-per-inference trends. Longer time windows and anchors to archived anomalies.

Alerting heuristics (starter rules):
- Latency SLO breach: rolling 5m p99 > SLO_threshold (auto-annotate with known deployments). Pager only for sustained 15m breach.
- Cache degradation: kv_cache.hit_rate drop > 15% vs 1h baseline => Pager to ops if traffic-weighted cost delta > $X/hour.
- Error spike: error.rate > 3x baseline AND absolute > 0.5% over 10m -> page.
- Cost spike: derived cost per token anomaly using seasonal baseline (z-score > 4) -> Op alert but not immediate page.

Sampling budget calculator (simple heuristic):
- Live storage cap target: 5TB/month for observability pipeline by default.
- Estimate per-sample sizes: full trace ~120KB, sampled trace ~18KB, metric point ~0.5KB.
- If request volume = 200M/day, 1% sampling of traces -> 2M traces/day -> ~36GB/day for sampled traces. Tune down for hosted tiers.

Privacy and Private deployments:
- Must support configuration switches to remove prompt text, PII fields, or to reduce trace retention by customer policy. Provide an API knob on the control plane to set tenant-level retention and sampling policies.
- KAnonymization: where tenant-level re-identification risk exists, only store tenant_bucket or aggregate.

Operational playbook snippets (how to reconstruct an incident):
1) Use operator pane to identify affected model.family and tenant_bucket.
2) Filter p99 heatmap and expand to last 30m traces.
3) If traces are missing, check synthetic probe bookmarks and query Archive for trace bookmarks matching request_id.
4) If prompt content is necessary, escalate to data access flow with justification (audit log attached).

Migration plan (6 week runway):
- Week 0-1: Finalize naming rules and tag buckets; create server-side metrics transforms.
- Week 2-3: Implement severity-weighted sampling and default tenant_bucket hashing in runtime.
- Week 4: Hook dashboards to new metric names and add deprecation warnings for legacy metrics.
- Week 5: Run dual-write for Live tier; compare costs.
- Week 6: Flip default retention; archive old indices after validation.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Archive fidelity: how many trace bookmarks per incident should be kept? (Proposal: keep up to 5 per major incident, TTL 1y)
- Tenant bucketing granularity: 256 vs 1024 buckets — tradeoff cardinality vs debugging utility.
- Cost cap for hosted free tier: define default sampling lower bound.

Next steps and owners:
- Review this doc with SRE and Serving Runtime (owner: Rina) by 2025-02-01.
- Implement tenant_bucket hashing PR (owner: Liam) by 2025-02-14.
- Add retention-policy UI knobs to Control Plane backlog (owner: Maya, linked PR above).

Notes / references:
- Related Confluence: OBS-SIGNAL-STEWARD-2025 (linked).
- Cost model spreadsheet: see attached internal sheet (billing-derived estimates).
- Compliance: coordinate with Security for Private deployment SLAs.

Quick appendix: example metric def (human-readable)
- name: inference.request.latency_ms.p95
- description: 95th percentile of end-to-end response latency in milliseconds measured at the ingress service.
- unit: ms
- tags: model.family, route, tenant_bucket, region
- retention: Live 7d full, Medium 90d aggregated by day, Archive 3y monthly rollup

If this direction looks good I will convert into a shorter checklist for SDK/runtime authors and draft the server-side transform PR template. Comments inline welcome.
